headline: Protect this tree. Save Africa's rainforests.
meta_description: The ogbono tree is key to African rainforests and cuisine. Sustainable harvesting of forest products can preserve these ecosystems.
summary_short: Africa's iconic ogbono tree feeds ecosystems and cuisines alike. A new series explores how sustainable harvesting keeps rainforests alive.
body:
The ogbono tree stands as one of Africa's most important plants, its seeds woven into the fabric of African cooking and forest life alike. This towering canopy tree does far more than feed people—it shelters countless species and anchors the rainforests across the continent. Yet these forests face mounting pressure. A new four-part series, produced through a collaboration between The Rainforester and Mongabay, reveals a different path forward: sustainable harvesting of non-timber forest products, or NTFPs, as a way to keep rainforests standing and thriving.

The premise is simple but powerful. Rather than clearing forests for timber or agriculture, communities can harvest forest products that regenerate—foods, medicines, fibers—while preserving the ecosystem intact. The ogbono tree exemplifies this possibility. Its seeds are treasured in African cuisine, yet harvesting them doesn't require felling the tree or destroying the forest around it. When done thoughtfully, this kind of harvesting creates economic incentive to protect rather than cut.

What makes this approach compelling is that it addresses a real tension: forests need protection, but people who live near them need livelihoods. The series explores how sustainable NTFP harvesting bridges that gap, allowing communities to benefit from their forests while keeping them alive for future generations and the wildlife that depends on them. It's a reminder that conservation isn't about locking forests away from people—it's about finding ways for people and forests to thrive together.
quick_facts: Ogbono is one of Africa's most iconic plants
Its seed is a staple ingredient in African cuisine
A four-part series explores sustainable forest harvesting with The Rainforester and Mongabay
The tree provides food and shelter for many rainforest species
Non-timber forest products can keep ecosystems alive while supporting communities
